verdict.rationale: Stagehand's user-data best-practices page documents a persistent user data directory. It survives browser shutdown, so the next run starts from the same cookies and local storage. For Browserbase sessions, contexts persist browser data, which together deliver reusable logged-in state across runs. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of skipping login walls or managing multiple named profiles, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can persist logged-in browser state in reusable profiles so agents skip the login wall on every subsequent run

citations.quote: Stagehand creates the directory if it does not exist and leaves it in place after the browser shuts down, so the next run starts from the same cookies and local storage
For Browserbase sessions, use contexts to persist browser data
